title: Build a calculator as a single static HTML file named `index.html` in the repo r...
statement:
Build a calculator as a single static HTML file named `index.html` in the repo root.

Requirements:
- A display, and a keypad of buttons: digits 0-9, a decimal point, the four operators
  (add, subtract, multiply, divide), equals, and clear.
- Pressing digits builds the current entry and shows it in the display. Pressing 1 then 2
  then 3 shows `123`. The decimal point adds a decimal point to the entry; an entry can
  contain at most one.
- A number, an operator, a second number, then equals shows the result. `7 + 8 =` shows `15`.
- Clear (AC) resets everything. The display shows `0`.
- The di...

title: Build a single-file calculator
statement: Build a calculator as a single static HTML file named index.html in the repo root with display, keypad (digits 0-9, decimal point, four operators, equals, clear), digit entry, decimal handling, arithmetic, and reset functionality.
acceptance: index.html file created in repo root
Display element present with data-testid='calc-display'
Digit buttons 0-9 with data-testid='key-0' through 'key-9'
Decimal point button with data-testid='key-dot'
Operator buttons (+, -, *, /) with data-testid='key-add', 'key-sub', 'key-mul', 'key-div'
Equals button with data-testid='key-equals'
Clear button with data-testid='key-clear'
Pressing digits builds entry and shows in display (1 2 3 → 123)
Decimal point adds to entry, maximum one per entry
Arithmetic sequence (number, operator, number, equals) produces correct result (7 + 8 = 15)
sub_requirements: Display and keypad UI with correct test attributes
Digit entry and display behavior
Decimal point handling (max one)
Arithmetic operations and equals
Clear/reset functionality
Single-file, offline-first implementation

title: Add chained calculations.
statement:
Add chained calculations.

- Pressing an operator while an operation is already waiting applies that waiting operation
  first and shows the running result. After `2 + 3`, pressing the multiply key shows `5`.
- Any number of operations can be chained before equals. `1 + 2 + 3 + 4 =` shows `10`.

Decision — how expressions are evaluated. This holds for the rest of the project:
- The calculator uses immediate execution. Each operator key finishes the operation already
  waiting, strictly left to right. There is no operator precedence.
  `2 + 3 × 4 =` is `20`, not `14`.
- Reason: this is how a po...

title: Add chained calculations
statement: The calculator must support chained calculations where operators execute immediately left-to-right, and pressing an operator while one is waiting shows the running result.
acceptance: Pressing an operator while an operation is waiting applies that operation first and shows the running result (e.g., after 2 + 3, pressing multiply shows 5)
Any number of operations can be chained before equals (e.g., 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = shows 10)
Calculator uses immediate execution with no operator precedence (e.g., 2 + 3 × 4 = shows 20, not 14)
sub_requirements: Pressing an operator applies waiting operation and shows running result
Multiple operations can be chained in sequence
Immediate execution model with strict left-to-right evaluation

title: Two things: how numbers are shown, and division by zero.
statement:
Two things: how numbers are shown, and division by zero.

Decision — number presentation. This holds for the rest of the project:
- Round the displayed number to at most 10 significant digits.
- Drop trailing zeros after the decimal point, and drop a trailing decimal point.
  `1 ÷ 8 =` shows `0.125`. `4 ÷ 2 =` shows `2`. `2 ÷ 3 =` shows `0.6666666667`.
- No thousands separators. Use exponential notation only when the magnitude is 1e10 or
  larger, or smaller than 1e-9.
- The rounding happens only when the number is rendered. The value the calculator stores and
  computes with is never rounded,...

title: Number display formatting and division by zero
statement: Numbers are displayed with specific formatting rules; division by zero enters an error state that blocks further input.
acceptance: Results rounded to at most 10 significant digits at render time only
Trailing zeros dropped after decimal point; trailing decimal point dropped
No thousands separators; exponential notation only for |magnitude| ≥ 1e10 or < 1e-9
data-value attribute always carries exact unrounded value
While typing, display shows entry exactly as typed
Division by zero (or any non-finite result) displays 'Error'
Error state blocks all input except clear
Clear resets error state and display to '0'
data-error attribute always set to 'true' or 'false'
sub_requirements: Number presentation: rounding, significant digits, format rules
Division by zero: error state and input blocking

title: Add two single-key operations. Each acts on the current entry immediately.
statement:
Add two single-key operations. Each acts on the current entry immediately.

- `data-testid="key-sign"` — a `±` key that flips the sign of the current entry.
  `5 ±` shows `-5`, and pressing it again shows `5`.
- `data-testid="key-percent"` — a `%` key that divides the current entry by 100.
  `50 %` shows `0.5`.

title: Add two single-key operations
statement: The calculator must support ± and % keys that act on the current entry immediately.
acceptance: ±key (data-testid='key-sign') flips the sign of the current entry: 5±→-5, ±→5
% key (data-testid='key-percent') divides the current entry by 100: 50%→0.5
While typing a number, ± flips the text and allows typing to continue
On a finished result, both ± and % make the new value the right operand if an operator is waiting (2+50%=gives 2.5)
After ± or %, the next digit starts a new number
Keyboard layout updated to standard: AC ± % ÷ / 7 8 9 × / 4 5 6 − / 1 2 3 + / 0 . =
sub_requirements: Implement ± key that flips sign of current entry
Implement % key that divides current entry by 100
Define behavior when each key is pressed during typing vs on a result

title: Add parentheses, so a user can group part of a calculation.
statement:
Add parentheses, so a user can group part of a calculation.

- `data-testid="key-lparen"` — the `(` key
- `data-testid="key-rparen"` — the `)` key
- `2 + ( 3 × 4 ) =` is `14`.
- `( 2 + 3 ) × 4 =` is `20`.
- Groups can be nested.

title: Add parentheses for grouping calculations
statement: A user can group part of a calculation using parentheses, with nested groups supported.
acceptance: ( key with data-testid="key-lparen" exists
) key with data-testid="key-rparen" exists
2 + ( 3 × 4 ) = evaluates to 14
( 2 + 3 ) × 4 = evaluates to 20
Nested groups work correctly
Outside groups, calculator still works left-to-right as before

title: The `%` key is generating support tickets. People expect it to mean "percent of ...
statement:
The `%` key is generating support tickets. People expect it to mean "percent of the other
number" and it does not. Take the `%` key off the keypad.

Keep `±`. That one is fine and we still need it.

title: Remove percent key from calculator
statement: The `%` key must be removed from the calculator keypad because users expect it to mean "percent of the other number" and it does not.
acceptance: The `%` button element removed from the keypad HTML
The `percent()` function removed from the JavaScript
The event handler for `key-percent` removed from the click dispatcher
The AC button widened to span the space previously occupied by the `%` key
The `±` key and its functionality preserved unchanged
sub_requirements: Remove the `%` key from the keypad display
Remove the percent functionality code
Keep the `±` key working
Maintain keypad layout without empty gaps

title: Add a running tape of past calculations.
statement:
Add a running tape of past calculations.

- `data-testid="calc-tape"` — the tape container
- `data-testid="tape-row"` — one past calculation
- `data-testid="tape-expr"` — the expression, inside the row
- `data-testid="tape-result"` — its result, inside the row. Like `calc-display`, it also
  carries `data-value`, holding the exact result value as a plain number string, as
  produced by `String(value)`.
- `data-testid="tape-clear"` — a button that empties the tape

- A row is added each time equals completes a calculation. Newest row first.
- A row shows the expression and its result. Nothing e...

title: Running tape of past calculations
statement: Add a running tape that records past calculations, showing expression and result, with newest entries first and a clear button.
acceptance: Tape container with data-testid='calc-tape' renders above display
Each completed calculation adds a tape-row with data-testid='tape-row' showing expression and result
Expression appears in tape-expr element with data-testid='tape-expr'
Result appears in tape-result element with data-testid='tape-result' carrying data-value as plain number string from String(value)
Clear button with data-testid='tape-clear' empties tape without changing display
Newest rows appear first in tape
Only real calculations triggered by equals add rows: Error states and lone numbers add nothing
Operator replacement on fresh state shows only final operator on tape
Sign flip on groups displays as -( ... ) on tape
sub_requirements: Tape UI structure with container, rows, expression and result elements
Tape row generation on equals completion
Expression and result capture with exact formatting
Clear button functionality
Newest-first ordering
Error and single-number filtering

title: Bug report from a user:
statement:
Bug report from a user:

"The tape prints ugly numbers. I did 0.1 + 0.2 — the display showed 0.3, which is right, but
the line it wrote on the tape says 0.30000000000000004. Same thing with 1 ÷ 3: the display
looks fine and the tape is a mess. It's the same calculation. It should read the same in
both places."

Reproduce it and fix it.

title: Add memory keys.
statement:
Add memory keys.

- `data-testid="key-mplus"` — M+, adds the value currently displayed to memory.
- `data-testid="key-mr"` — MR, recalls the memory value into the display.
- `data-testid="key-mc"` — MC, clears memory back to zero.
- `data-testid="mem-indicator"` — shows whether memory is holding anything. It carries
  `data-active="true"` when memory is non-zero and `data-active="false"` when it is zero.

Memory starts at zero. Make sure memory respects the number behaviour we agreed on.

title: Add memory keys
statement: The calculator must provide M+, MR, and MC memory keys plus a memory indicator that shows whether memory holds a non-zero value.
acceptance: M+ key (data-testid="key-mplus") adds the displayed value to memory as exact value, not rounded
MR key (data-testid="key-mr") recalls memory value into the display
MC key (data-testid="key-mc") clears memory to zero
Memory indicator (data-testid="mem-indicator") displays with data-active="true" when memory is non-zero and data-active="false" when zero
M+ displays Error and preserves memory on overflow
Memory keys do nothing in error state
AC leaves memory unchanged
Memory respects exact value storage with rounding only at display time
sub_requirements: Implement M+ button that adds displayed value to memory
Implement MR button that recalls memory value
Implement MC button that clears memory
Implement memory indicator with active state attribute

title: Final pass.
statement:
Final pass.

Keyboard entry:
- Digit keys and `.` type into the entry.
- `+`, `-`, `*`, `/` are the four operators.
- `Enter` or `=` is equals.
- `Escape` is clear.

Compact scientific mode:
- `data-testid="key-sci"` — a key that toggles a small scientific panel.
- While the panel is open it offers `data-testid="key-sqrt"` (√x), `data-testid="key-square"`
  (x²) and `data-testid="key-recip"` (1/x). Each acts on the current entry immediately:
  `9 √` shows `3`.

Then verify that nothing we built in earlier steps has broken, and fix anything that has.

title: Final pass: keyboard entry and scientific panel
statement: Add keyboard entry for digits, operators, equals and clear, and a compact scientific panel with √x, x², and 1/x functions.
acceptance: Digit keys and `.` type into the entry
`+`, `-`, `*`, `/` are operators via keyboard
`Enter` or `=` executes equals via keyboard
`Escape` clears via keyboard
Shortcuts using Ctrl, Cmd or Alt pass through to browser
Pressing `Enter` while a button has focus does not also press that button
`data-testid="key-sci"` toggles the scientific panel open and closed
Panel starts closed
`data-testid="key-sqrt"` (√x) acts on current entry immediately
`data-testid="key-square"` (x²) acts on current entry immediately
sub_requirements: Keyboard entry for calculation
Compact scientific mode with three functions
Verification that no earlier steps broke
